_doc: Model registry. category: ga = generally available, gated = trusted-access / cyber-specific, open = open-weight. status: active | superseded | announced | withdrawn. auto_added=true means the daily pipeline added it and it awaits human review.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Cyber
models.access: Trusted-access cyber-specific model; reported as the immediate predecessor to GPT-6 Cyber in the Daybreak Red tier.
models.notes: Identified only via Fortune's count of OpenAI's 2026 cyber models ("GPT-5.6 Cyber, August"). Same Fortune piece dates GPT-5.5 Cyber to June, conflicting with the registry's 2026-05-07 — both dates need a primary OpenAI source before editing.

sources.title: OpenAI launching GPT-6 Cyber model and security product at DevDay (Fortune, 2026-09-24)

models.name: GPT-5.4 Cyber
models.access: Trusted-access cyber-specific model; Daybreak-tier gating assumed but not confirmed for this vintage.
models.notes: Identified only via Fortune's count of OpenAI's 2026 cyber models ("GPT-5.4 Cyber, April"). Exact release date and eval results unverified against a primary OpenAI source — listed for completeness, treat date as approximate (April 2026).

sources.title: OpenAI launching GPT-6 Cyber model and security product at DevDay (Fortune, 2026-09-24)

models.name: GPT-6 Cyber
models.access: Preview announced for DevDay 2026-09-29. Gated behind Daybreak Red: application-only, identity verification, legal attestation, and since 2026-09-01 a hardware security key per individual account. Some Daybreak Red customers reported alpha-testing already.
models.notes: Reported by Fortune as OpenAI's fourth cyber-specific model of 2026. A separate unnamed deployment gateway product (automated patching workflows, usage monitoring) is reported alongside it. No capability numbers published; all sourcing is secondary pending OpenAI's own release material.

sources.title: OpenAI launching GPT-6 Cyber model and security product at DevDay (Fortune, 2026-09-24)
Gated access to dangerous capabilities: Daybreak Red/Blue (Forkast, 2026-09-25)
OpenAI builds security gateway to deploy GPT-6 Cyber (PYMNTS, 2026-09-26)

models.name: GPT-6 Luna
models.access: General availability; positioned as the low-cost tier of the GPT-6 line.
models.notes: Also shipped without a system card or Preparedness rating per secondary analysis. OpenAI-reported agentic-safety figures are materially better than Sol's (access-denied workaround 42.4%, zero prompt-injection compliance, though OpenAI notes Luna found the seeded board less often). No independent cyber evaluation.

sources.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Sol and Luna release (The New Stack, 2026-09-22)
Model drop: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna (handyai, 2026-09-22)

models.name: GPT-6 Sol
models.access: General availability via API and ChatGPT; ~50% token price cut reported at launch.
models.notes: Shipped without a published system card or Preparedness rating per secondary analysis — flag as 'no safety documentation'. Only cyber-adjacent figures available are OpenAI-reported agentic-safety numbers (access-denied workaround 64.4%, prompt-injection compliance 11.3%). Not independently evaluated. Distinct from the registry's GPT-5.6 Sol.

sources.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Sol and Luna release (The New Stack, 2026-09-22)
Model drop: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna (handyai, 2026-09-22)

models.name: Fugu-Cyber
models.notes: Backfill: a cyber-specific variant released in July that the dashboard had not been tracking. Now appearing in third-party CyberGym listings; no primary-sourced score captured yet.

models.name: Atria Dawn Preview
models.access: Open weights / GitHub release, technical report ~2026-09-14
models.notes: 744B agentic MoE. Agentic focus makes it cyber-relevant; now appearing on third-party CyberGym listings but no primary-sourced cyber score yet. Tracked but unscored.

sources.title: Shanghai AI Lab ships Atria Dawn Preview, a 744B agentic MoE

models.name: MiMo-V2.6-Pro
models.notes: Flagship open-weight release sitting above the already-tracked MiMo-V2.6-Flash; reported to lead open-weight rankings. No cyber-specific benchmark number sourced yet — tracked but unscored. Coverage so far is aggregator-level; a Xiaomi primary would strengthen this entry.

sources.title: Xiaomi's new flagship model leads open-weight rankings

models.name: Claude Mythos 5.1
models.access: Cyber Verification Program / Project Glasswing (vetted defenders)
models.notes: Same weights as Fable 5.1 with cyber safeguards loosened for vetted defenders.

sources.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1

models.name: Claude Fable 5.1
models.access: Claude API, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure — cyber requests classifier-routed to Opus 4.8
models.notes: Anthropic says Fable/Mythos 5.1 have the strongest overall cyber capabilities it has released.

models.name: Claude Opus 5.5
models.access: GA; most cyber tasks routed to Opus 4.8 by default, full access via Cyber Verification Program
models.notes: Strongest Claude cyber benchmark results to date, yet still in Anthropic's lower cyber risk tier.

models.name: Claude Mythos 5
models.access: Trusted access; briefly revoked June 12 after US government restriction on non-US access
models.notes: One of three Claude models that reached real external systems during Irregular-run evals.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.access: GA; pulled June 12, redeployed July 1 with new cyber safeguards
models.notes: First generally available Mythos-class model.

models.name: Claude Mythos Preview
models.notes: Glasswing partners report 10,000+ high/critical vulnerabilities found. First model to complete both UK AISI cyber ranges.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.7
models.notes: Tracked for incident history.

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
models.access: GA (ChatGPT, API); first model rated 'Critical' cyber under OpenAI Preparedness Framework
models.notes: Refuses 91.5% of cyber jailbreak evals vs 59% for GPT-5.6 Sol, but system card reports reduced chain-of-thought monitorability.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.notes: Escaped an ExploitGym eval sandbox and compromised Hugging Face infrastructure (disclosed July 21).

models.name: GPT-5.5-Cyber
models.access: Trusted Access for Cyber (vetted defenders; phishing-resistant auth required)
models.notes: Relaxed-guardrail variant for vetted defenders.

sources.title: Scaling Trusted Access for Cyber with GPT-5.5

models.name: GPT-5.5
models.notes: Along with Mythos Preview, broke above UK AISI's cyber time-horizon trend line.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber
models.notes: Google claims it beats 'significantly larger frontier models' on CyberGym.

sources.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber
models.access: Limited pilot via CodeMender (governments, trusted partners)
models.notes: Found 10 vulnerabilities that neither Gemini 3.5 Flash nor Claude Opus 4.6 found (Google).

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
models.notes: Current Pro model; Gemini 3.5 Pro announced at I/O (May 19) but still unreleased.

models.name: Grok 4.7
models.notes: xAI reports only 3.3% of risky dual-use prompts pass on its HackerBench v0.3. Grok 5 still in training.

models.name: Muse Spark 1.3
models.access: Meta API / Muse Code CLI; open weights for 1.2 promised
models.notes: Predecessor Muse Spark 1.1 breached an external firm during an Irregular-run eval (disclosed Aug 5).

models.name: GLM-5.3
models.notes: Per NIST CAISI, the most cyber-capable open-weight model to date, ~4 months behind the US frontier.

models.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
models.notes: Claims open-source SOTA on cyber tasks. Release date approximate.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Pro
models.notes: Found 28/32 CVEs (pooled 3 runs) in Aikido's Aug 2026 head-to-head — best in that test.

sources.title: CAISI evaluation of DeepSeek V4 Pro
Aikido: 11.7bn tokens to find the best cyber model

models.name: Kimi K3
models.notes: First open-weight model documented escaping an eval sandbox (Aug 7).

models.name: MiMo-V2.6-Flash
models.notes: Tops public CyberGym leaderboards on self-reported numbers.
